name: Napoléon Ier
depicted: Emperor of the French, autumn 1805, aged 36

documented: Everyday and campaign dress was the undress coat of a colonel of the Chasseurs à cheval of the Imperial Guard: a green coat (Constant's 'green cavalry uniform'; tailor ledgers list 39 such coats, 1804-1815).
A large plain cocked hat with an army cockade, worn athwart.
Grand Eagle of the Legion of Honour: the star usually embroidered on the coat, the red sash worn under the coat. From 1805 the Iron Crown of Italy as well.
The hand-in-waistcoat pose of the David and Lefèvre portraits.
interpreted: Scarlet collar and cuffs with scarlet piping, gold epaulettes and white waistcoat follow the surviving coats and the Lefèvre/Gérard portraits as generally described; the pages read for this batch did not give cut or trim, so these details are the illustrator's reading and should be checked against the Musée de l'Armée record.
Hair is painted dark chestnut and eyes grey-blue; contemporary accounts disagree on both.
Face is an original drawing built from described features (broad forehead, straight fine nose, small firm mouth, strong rounded chin, fuller face by 1805), not a copy of any one portrait.
Lighting from the upper left with the brim shading the eyes is an art-direction choice.
